subject: POC workshop — ops, prompt routing, surge rehearsal (scheduling + follow-ups)
messages:
From: Jordan Alvarez <jordan@bluebridge.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC workshop — ops scope and proposed dates

Hi Soojin / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Bluebridge is ready to move to an interactive POC. We want a hands-on session that covers: prompt review (our 30+ templates), routing/priority lanes for low-latency serving, and a short surge load rehearsal for realistic traffic spikes.

Goal: validate routing policies and make sure 95th percentile latency stays under 250ms for our vanity prompts; surface any prompt-level regressions. Estimated time: 2 hours + a 30m follow-up.

Available windows next week (PST):
- Tue Nov 6, 10:00–13:00
- Wed Nov 7, 09:00–12:00

Can you confirm what you need from us (configs, prompt list, IP allowlist)? Also: who from Redwood should we expect in the call (engineering + solutions)?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Alvarez
Sr. Product Manager, Bluebridge
jordan@bluebridge.com
+1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: POC workshop — ops scope and proposed dates

Hi Jordan — great to hear the team is ready. We're aligned on the scope. Quick answers up front:
- What we'll need from you: full prompt set (CSV or spreadsheet), a small representative traffic trace (if available), and IP ranges for allowlisting the test harness.
- Redwood attendees: Soojin (solutions), Dev (infra/serving), Marcus (performance), Laura (CS).

We have two viable windows this week: Thu Nov 2 09:30–12:00 PST (short notice) or Mon Nov 6 10:00–13:00 PST. If you can do Thu Nov 2 we can run an extended hands-on + a light surge rehearsal and still iterate the week after. If Nov 6 is a hard constraint, we can do a prep-run on Nov 2 internally and then the joint session on the 6th.

I've attached a short POC runbook and an outline of the session so you can see the planned exercises.

Proposed agenda (2.5h total)
- 0:00–0:20 intro & success metrics
- 0:20–1:10 prompt review + mapping to routing lanes
- 1:10–1:40 live serving checks (latency profiling)
- 1:40–2:10 surge rehearsal (configured spikes)
- 2:10–2:30 action items & immediate next steps

If Thu Nov 2 works for you, please confirm and send the prompt spreadsheet and any tracelog. Otherwise confirm Nov 6 and we'll schedule the prep run.

Best,
So 

--

Subject: Re: POC workshop — ops scope and proposed dates

Looping in infra notes for the session — copied below and attaching the surge test config.

Key infra asks (please send to Bluebridge):
- A trimmed prompt sample (max 200 prompts) in CSV with a column for expected priority (high, normal, low)
- A representative QPS curve (if you have it) or expected peak QPS for the rehearsal
- IP ranges for allowlist and a contact for firewall windows

Planned infra setup for Thu Nov 2 (if confirmed):
- Dedicated cluster: 4x A100-equivalent nodes (reserved for the rehearsal window)
- Routing lanes: two lanes (fast-path, economical) with automatic fallback to smaller-quantized model for burst overrides
- KV cache prefixing enabled for prompt groups marked as 'high' priority
- Surge tool: will replay mixes from the provided CSV and add an artificial spike (4x baseline) for 3 minutes to validate circuit-breaker policies

I attached surge_test_config.yaml — it contains beam sizes, concurrency targets, and expected SLO thresholds. If Bluebridge expects higher concurrency, increase the concurrency targets column.

- Dev

Attachments: surge_test_config.yaml

Thanks — Thu Nov 2 works for our core team. Small ask: can we shift start to 10:00 PST (we have a product sync at 09:00). Also — we'll prioritize a 120-prompt set (CSV & expected priority) and a QPS trace; I'll send both by EOD today.

One priority for the session: we want a short segment that compares latency on the fast-path vs fallback when the KV cache hits and misses — maybe 10–15 minutes with a scripted example. Can Dev allocate time to walk through tracing and explain root-cause signals if a lane starts to degrade?

Looking forward, and thanks for the runbook.

Jordan
